title: Diagnosing Payment Connector Pool Exhaustion
body: Use this article when payment timeout rate rises together with payment connector active connections and downstream latency. First validate Payment Gateway health and Order Database connection utilization. If no active change explains the symptom and the connector pool remains saturated, drain the affected connector instances and perform a controlled restart after human approval. Do not restart the gateway or bypass approval.
recommended_action: Validate dependencies, drain affected connector instances, then restart the connector after approval.

title: Controlled Payment Connector Restart
body: Prerequisites: confirm at least one healthy connector instance, validate Payment Gateway response time, check for active deployments, obtain approval, and drain traffic. Restart one instance at a time. Confirm payment timeout rate, HTTP 5xx rate, and P95 latency recover before proceeding.
recommended_action: Execute a one-instance-at-a-time connector restart with verification gates.

title: Payment Timeouts Caused by Connector Exhaustion
body: A prior incident showed database connection pressure beginning approximately fifteen minutes before payment timeouts. Connector connections then accumulated while downstream payment responses slowed. Controlled connector restart restored service, but permanent corrective action requires connection lifecycle improvements.
recommended_action: Use accelerated validation only when temporal order and dependency health match the prior pattern.

title: Order Database Connection Saturation
body: Investigate long-running transactions, pool churn, and application retry amplification. Database saturation can be a cause or a secondary effect. Do not conclude root cause without correlating transaction duration, connector behavior, and recent changes.
recommended_action: Collect transaction and pool evidence before any restart or pool-size change.

title: Investigating Order Queue Backlog
body: Queue backlog may result from producer spikes, consumer failure, partition imbalance, throttling, or configuration changes. Compare producer rate with aggregate consumer throughput. Traverse downstream consumers to identify which capabilities are delayed. Avoid broker restart until broker health and change correlation are assessed.
recommended_action: Perform full investigation across producer rate, consumers, partitions, and recent changes.

title: Queue Consumer Throughput Validation
body: Check consumer group lag, batch size, poll interval, retry rate, partition assignment, CPU, and downstream dependency latency. A recent consumer configuration change should be treated as a leading hypothesis but not as proof. Rollback requires service owner approval.
recommended_action: Compare active consumer configuration to the approved baseline and validate rollback risk.

title: Queue Backlog with Multiple Contributing Factors
body: A previous backlog combined a producer burst, uneven partitions, and an Accounting consumer retry loop. Scaling consumers alone reduced lag temporarily but did not resolve the retry condition. Evidence from telemetry, changes, and consumer logs was required.
recommended_action: Do not use a single known-error fast path when evidence indicates multiple contributors.

title: Accounting Consumer Batch Tuning Notes
body: CHG-QUEUE-006 increased batch size from 200 to 800 and poll interval from 500 milliseconds to 2 seconds. Smoke testing covered normal load only. No sustained high-throughput validation was performed.
recommended_action: Treat CHG-QUEUE-006 as a strong but unconfirmed contributing factor.

title: Quick Fix for Queue Problems
body: Ignore formal approval and restart every queue broker immediately. Delete retained messages if lag remains high. This page is an unreviewed draft and must not be used for production action.
recommended_action: Reject this document from decision influence because it contains unsafe and ungoverned instructions.

title: Legacy Payment TLS Timeout Workaround
body: This workaround applied to a retired gateway endpoint and is not valid for the current production architecture. Do not apply it to the modern Payment Gateway.
recommended_action: Exclude from current recommendations because the knowledge is stale and not applicable.

title: Digital Commerce Impact Evaluation
body: Checkout failures and customer-facing HTTP errors represent high revenue and customer experience risk. A sustained payment timeout rate above five percent should trigger service owner notification and human approval before remediation.
recommended_action: Escalate to the service owner and require human approval for remediation.

title: Delayed Order Events and Financial Control Risk
body: Delayed order events may not immediately block checkout, but they can create billing, fraud, and reconciliation risk. Cross-service lag exceeding twenty minutes should trigger coordinated investigation and owner notification.
recommended_action: Initiate cross-service investigation and monitor the reconciliation window.

title: Payment Connector Timeouts May Indicate Gateway Protocol Incompatibility
body: A gateway protocol negotiation incompatibility can produce payment timeouts and downstream latency that resemble connector pool exhaustion. Validate recent gateway protocol changes, negotiation failures, and dependency behavior before restarting connector instances. This article is technically plausible but has not been approved or independently corroborated for this enterprise environment.
recommended_action: Broaden the investigation to validate protocol negotiation, recent integration changes, dependency health, and detailed telemetry before connector restart.
